home.title: Twelve courses of silence.
home.tagline: A kaiseki omakase journey through Edomae tradition, served at the counter.

menu.title: Chef's progression.
menu.intro: Twelve courses, twenty-two seats, one nightly service. The menu evolves with the season — every nigiri pressed by hand in front of you.

sakizuke.name: Sakizuke — The Welcome
sakizuke.description: A small sake cup cradling a single seasonal bite. Tonight: dashi jelly, yuzu zest, and a single Hokkaido scallop.

mukozuke.name: Mukozuke — The Sashimi
mukozuke.description: Three slices of bluefin tuna — akami, chu-toro, o-toro — arranged on a hand-formed ice bowl, served with freshly grated wasabi.

wanmono.name: Wanmono — The Soup
wanmono.description: Clear dashi poured at the table over a poached fillet of gindara and a single shiitake. The broth is forty-eight hours in the making.

hassun.name: Hassun — The Eight Bites
hassun.description: Eight small preparations representing the season: simmered octopus, miso-pickled cucumber, salt-grilled ayu, and five more — each a sentence in a poem.
hassun.ingredients: Octopus · ayu · cucumber · five seasonal bites

mizumono.name: Mizumono — The Cold Bowl
mizumono.description: Cherry tomatoes marinated in rice vinegar, served on ice with shiso and a single drop of olive oil pressed at the counter.

nimono.name: Nimono — The Simmered
nimono.description: A five-hour simmer of wagyu cheek, daikon, and carrot in a soy-mirin glaze. Served in a hand-thrown Kyoto bowl.

yakimono.name: Yakimono — The Grilled
yakimono.description: Mentaiko-grilled black cod over a cedar leaf, brushed with sweet soy at the counter. The fish arrives whole, filleted tableside.

shiizakana.name: Shiizakana — The Strong
shiizakana.description: A small plate of unagi glazed in tare, served with sansho pepper and a quail egg yolk broken at the table.

sushi.name: Omae-sushi — The Five Pieces
sushi.description: Five nigiri, pressed at the counter in front of you: kanpachi, hamachi, madai, botan-ebi, and uni from Hokkaido. Warm rice, cool fish.

takiawase.name: Takiawase — The Garden
takiawase.description: Seasonal vegetables briefly blanched and dressed with sesame. A small pause between the fish and what comes next.

tomewan.name: Tomewan — The Last Soup
tomewan.description: Akadashi red miso, served in a lacquered bowl with a small mound of rice on the side. The final warm course before dessert.

mizumochi.name: Mizumochi — The Conclusion
mizumochi.description: A single peach mochi served on a hand-pressed ice spoon, with hojicha poured tableside. The meal ends in quiet.

story.title: Twenty-two seats. One counter.
story.p1: Chef Aiko Tanaka trained for fourteen years in Tokyo before opening Kaiseki São Paulo in 2019. She sources fish daily from the Tsukiji outer market — flown overnight, served the same day.
story.p2: The restaurant seats twenty-two. There is no menu printed on paper. Each guest receives the same twelve-course progression, with one substitution offered for allergies.
story.p3: Tanaka-san works the counter alone. She presses every nigiri in front of the guest. The room falls quiet when she begins a course. Conversations resume when the plate is set down.
story.p4: The waitlist is six weeks. Reservations open on the first Monday of every month at 10:00 BRT. The phone is answered in Portuguese, English, or Japanese.
story.ctaTitle: The next service is on Friday.

reserve.title: By WhatsApp.
reserve.body: All requests are answered within 24 hours. Please include the requested date, party size, and any dietary restrictions.
reserve.note: Opens with a pre-filled message in your language.
reserve.message: Hello! I would like to reserve at Kaiseki São Paulo — Kaiseki omakase for [N] guests on [DATE]. Thank you!
